result.title: Passing Tests, Missing Semantics: Evidence of Interpretive Lock-In in Plan-Based DataFrame Code Generation
result.comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER 2026)
result.summary: Planning and revision are intended to bring generated code closer to the task specification. Yet a mistaken interpretation can persist across the plan, implementation, and tests - a pattern we call interpretive lock-in. We investigate this risk on 30 DataFrame tasks derived from TPC Benchmark DS, comparing Frozen One-Pass, Test-Guided Revision, and PlanAudit-Guided Revision. Test-pass counts rose from 22/30 to 29/30 and 30/30, yet no generated solution matched its stored reference output. Evaluator controls returned the expected outcome in 57/57 cases. Same-engine SQL re-execution reproduced 28/30 references; all 77 test-passing runs on these tasks still failed reference agreement. PlanAudit-Guided Revision improved code scores on 3/30 tasks and test coverage on 11/30, but the median paired change was zero for both measures. Failure analysis revealed tests that omitted requirements, adopted candidate-defined schemas, used nondiscriminating fixtures, or repeated the implementation's incorrect logic. Fresh generation on ten targeted tasks produced 0/30 reference matches and 25/25 false passes among test-passing runs. These findings are diagnostic rather than causal: the pipelines differ in feedback, grounding, call budgets, and editing permissions, and the study uses one model and one primary generation per eligible task. Because pre-adjudication human labels were not retained, inter-rater agreement cannot be reconstructed and the mechanism analyses remain exploratory. Overall, increasingly successful self-generated tests did not establish semantic correctness, even after excluding unreproduced references.

AI.brief_summary: 在 30 个基于 TPC-DS 的 DataFrame 任务上比较一次性生成、测试引导修订与计划审查引导修订，发现测试通过率从 22/30 升至 30/30，但无一解匹配参考输出，并将这种错误解释跨计划、实现与测试持续存在的现象称为「解释锁定」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「自生成测试通过≠语义正确」及评估器对照、非判别性测试的诊断线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中验证信号是否具判别力、视觉证据筛选与停止决策的收益判断。
